newsitem.title: UK: World oil output up 2.28 mbpd in four months - IEA.
newsitem.headline: World oil output up 2.28 mbpd in four months - IEA.

text.p: The growth in world oil supplies slowed down last month but on top of increases in the previous three months was enough to undermine oil prices, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
The IEA, in a monthly oil market report, estimated February world oil output grew by 340,000 barrels a day (bpd) to 74.79 million.
World oil production had shot up 2.28 million in the space of four months, the agency said.
With OPEC steady at 26.98 million bpd in February non-OPEC countries accounted for the supply increase.

"Although weather effects, field delays and technical problems in the North Sea and Australia have restricted oil production from a number of key fields so far this year, supplies from fields in other areas have more than compensated," the agency said.
"A substantial relaxation in global supply/demand fundamentals led to a steep decline in Atlantic Basin benchmark crude oil prices," it said
Non-OPEC supplies rose to 44.98 million bpd from 44.68 million in January and an average of 44.27 million in the fourth quarter of 1996, the agency esimated.
"Strong evidence of the underlying upward trend in non-OPEC supply remains, especially for offshore areas," the IEA said.
Year-on-year non-OPEC growth for 1997 is still expected to be 1.9 million bpd, despite some downward revisions to the IEA's North Sea forecast.
